LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD builds a Portuguese hyphenation dictionary from the official LibreOffice dictionaries repository on GitHub, which is the legitimate upstream source for this data. The workflow is standard VCS packaging: `prepare()` clones the declared upstream with a blob-filtered sparse checkout, limits the checkout to the `pt_PT` directory, and `package()` only installs static files (`hyph_pt_PT.dic`, a README, and a LICENSES file) into `$pkgdir` plus a symlink under `/usr/share/myspell/dicts/`. There are no downloads from unrelated hosts, no encoded or obfuscated commands, no `eval`/`curl | bash` patterns, and no operations touching files outside `$pkgdir` or exfiltrating local data.

Two hygiene notes, neither malicious: the empty `source`/`sha256sums` arrays mean the git dependency is not declared in `source` (the clone is done manually in `prepare()`), and `git pull --ff-only` in `prepare()` fetches unchecked content from the mutable `master` ref at build time, which weakens reproducibility. However, the remote is the package's own declared upstream, the pull is restricted to fast-forwards, and the fetched content is never executed — it is only installed as data files — so this does not rise to a supply-chain threat.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard VCS packaging from legitimate LibreOffice upstream; no malicious behavior.</summary>
</security_assessment>

This file is an `.SRCINFO` metadata file, which contains only declarative package information — no executable code, no scripts, and no commands of any kind. The fields are entirely standard: package name/description, version, URL, architecture, licenses, make dependencies (`git`), optional dependencies, and provides/conflicts entries.

The declared URL points to the LibreOffice dictionaries repository on GitHub, which is the appropriate and expected upstream source for Portuguese (European) hyphenation rules. The `makedepends = git` entry is consistent with the `-git` package naming convention, indicating a VCS source. There is nothing in this file that could execute code, exfiltrate data, download anything, or modify the system.

No obfuscation, no suspicious network requests, no file operations, and no deviations from standard AUR packaging metadata practices are present.
</details>
